## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g., BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the ranked result sets to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity. This approach addresses complementary strengths: lexical search excels at matching rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs), while vector search captures semantic intent and meaning. The merged results are often ranked using reciprocal rank fusion, which normalizes and combines scores from both retrieval methods.

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on mixed queries that combine rare identifiers with natural language intent. It has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) systems.

## Reciprocal Rank Fusion

Reciprocal rank fusion is a technique for merging two independently ranked result sets. It normalizes scores from different retrieval methods so they can be combined fairly, avoiding the dominance of one method's scoring scale over another.
